01133| ### Unsupported Metadata

01143| | `<script>`                    | Learn more about [using scripts](/docs/app/guides/scripts).                                                                                                                                                                                  |
01144| | `<link rel="stylesheet" />`   | `import` stylesheets directly in the layout or page itself.                                                                                                                                                                                  |
01145| | `<link rel="preload" />`      | Use [ReactDOM preload method](#link-relpreload)                                                                                                                                                                                              |
01146| | `<link rel="preconnect" />`   | Use [ReactDOM preconnect method](#link-relpreconnect)                                                                                                                                                                                        |

01149| ### Resource hints
01150| 
01151| The `<link>` element has a number of `rel` keywords that can be used to hint to the browser that an external resource is likely to be needed. The browser uses this information to apply preloading optimizations depending on the keyword.

01153| While the Metadata API doesn't directly support these hints, you can use new [`ReactDOM` methods](https://github.com/facebook/react/pull/26237) to safely insert them into the `<head>` of the document.

01155| ```tsx filename="app/preload-resources.tsx" switcher

01157|

01159| 
01160| export function PreloadResources() {
01161|   ReactDOM.preload('...', { as: '...' })
01162|   ReactDOM.preconnect('...', { crossOrigin: '...' })

01169| ```jsx filename="app/preload-resources.js" switcher
01170| 'use client'
01171| 
01172| import ReactDOM from 'react-dom'
01173| 
01174| export function PreloadResources() {
01175|   ReactDOM.preload('...', { as: '...' })
01176|   ReactDOM.preconnect('...', { crossOrigin: '...' })

01178| 
01179|   return '...'
01180| }

01184| 
01185| Start loading a resource early in the page rendering (browser) lifecycle. [MDN Docs](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/HTML/Attributes/rel/preload).

01188| ReactDOM.preload(href: string, options: { as: string })
01189| ```
01190| 
01191| ```html filename="<head> output" hideLineNumbers
01192| <link rel="preload" href="..." as="..." />
01193| ```
01194| 
01195| ##### `<link rel="preconnect">`
01196| 
01197| Preemptively initiate a connection to an origin. [MDN Docs](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/HTML/Attributes/rel/preconnect).
01198| 
01199| ```tsx
01200| ReactDOM.preconnect(href: string, options?: { crossOrigin?: string })
01201| ```
01202| 
01203| ```html filename="<head> output" hideLineNumbers
01204| <link rel="preconnect" href="..." crossorigin />
01205| ```
01206| 
01207| #### `<link rel="dns-prefetch">`
01208| 
01209| Attempt to resolve a domain name before resources get requested. [MDN Docs](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/HTML/Attributes/rel/dns-prefetch).
01210| 
01211| ```tsx

01220| >

01222| > - Next.js in-built features such as `next/font`, `next/image` and `next/script` automatically handle relevant resource hints.
01223| 
01224| ## Behavior
01225| 
01226| ### Default Fields
01227| 
01228| There are two default `meta` tags that are always added even if a route doesn't define metadata:
01229| 
01230| - The [meta charset tag](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/HTML/Element/meta#attr-charset) sets the character encoding for the website.
01231| - The [meta viewport tag](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/HTML/Viewport_meta_tag) sets the viewport width and scale for the website to adjust for different devices.
01232| 
01233| ```html
01234| <meta charset="utf-8" />
01235| <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1" />
01236| ```
01237| 
01238| > **Good to know**: You can overwrite the default [`viewport`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/generate-metadata#viewport) meta tag.
01239| 
01240| ### Streaming metadata
01241| 
01242| Streaming metadata allows Next.js to render and send the initial UI to the browser, without waiting for `generateMetadata` to complete.
01243| 
01244| When `generateMetadata` resolves, the resulting metadata tags are appended to the `<body>` tag. We have verified that metadata is interpreted correctly by bots that execute JavaScript and inspect the full DOM (e.g. `Googlebot`).
01245| 
01246| For **HTML-limited bots** that can’t execute JavaScript (e.g. `facebookexternalhit`), metadata continues to block page rendering. The resulting metadata will be available in the `<head>` tag.
01247| 
01248| Next.js automatically detects **HTML-limited bots** by looking at the User Agent header. You can use the [`htmlLimitedBots`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/htmlLimitedBots) option in your Next.js config file to override the default [User Agent list](https://github.com/vercel/next.js/blob/canary/packages/next/src/shared/lib/router/utils/html-bots.ts).
01249| 
01250| To fully disable streaming metadata:
01251| 
01252| ```ts filename="next.config.ts" switcher
01253| import type { NextConfig } from 'next'
01254| 
01255| const config: NextConfig = {
01256|   htmlLimitedBots: /.*/,
01257| }
01258| 
01259| export default config
01260| ```
01261| 
01262| ```js filename="next.config.js" switcher
01263| module.exports = {
01264|   htmlLimitedBots: /.*/,
01265| }
01266| ```
01267| 
01268| Streaming metadata improves perceived performance by reducing [TTFB](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Glossary/Time_to_first_byte) and can help lowering [LCP](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Glossary/Largest_contentful_paint) time.
01269| 
01270| Overriding `htmlLimitedBots` could lead to longer response times. Streaming metadata is an advanced feature, and the default should be sufficient for most cases.
01271| 
01272| ### With Cache Components
01273| 
01274| When [Cache Components](/docs/app/getting-started/caching) is enabled, `generateMetadata` follows the same rules as other components. If metadata accesses runtime data (`cookies()`, `headers()`, `params`, `searchParams`) or performs uncached data fetching, it defers to request time.
01275| 
01276| How Next.js handles this depends on the rest of your page:
01277| 
01278| - **If other parts also defer to request time**: Prerendering generates a static shell, and metadata streams in with other deferred content.
01279| - **If the page or layout is otherwise fully prerenderable**: Next.js requires an explicit choice: cache the data if possible, or signal that deferred rendering is intentional.
01280| 
01281| Streaming metadata at runtime while the rest of the page is fully prerenderable is not common. To ensure this behavior is intentional, an error is raised indicating which page or layout needs to be handled.
01282| 
01283| To resolve this, you have two options. If metadata depends on external data but not runtime data, use `use cache`:
01284| 
01285| ```tsx filename="app/page.tsx" highlight={2}
01286| export async function generateMetadata() {
01287|   'use cache'
01288|   const { title, description } = await db.query('site-metadata')
01289|   return { title, description }
01290| }
01291| ```
01292| 
01293| If metadata genuinely requires runtime data, add a dynamic marker component to your page:
01294| 
01295| ```tsx filename="app/page.tsx" highlight={11-14,19,31}
01296| import { Suspense } from 'react'
01297| import { cookies } from 'next/headers'
01298| import { connection } from 'next/server'
01299| 
01300| export async function generateMetadata() {
01301|   const token = (await cookies()).get('token')?.value
01302|   // ... use token to fetch personalized metadata
01303|   return { title: 'Personalized Title' }
01304| }
01305| 
01306| const Connection = async () => {
01307|   await connection()
01308|   return null
01309| }
01310| 
01311| async function DynamicMarker() {
01312|   return (
01313|     <Suspense>
01314|       <Connection />
01315|     </Suspense>
01316|   )
01317| }
01318| 
01319| export default function Page() {
01320|   // DO NOT place await connection() here
01321|   // doing so prevents the article tag content from
01322|   // being included in the static shell
01323|   return (
01324|     <>
01325|       <article>Static content</article>
01326|       <DynamicMarker />
01327|     </>
01328|   )
01329| }
01330| ```
01331| 
01332| The `DynamicMarker` component renders nothing but tells Next.js the page has intentional dynamic content. By wrapping it in Suspense, the static content still prerenders normally.
01333| 
01334| See [Next.js encountered runtime data in `generateMetadata()`](/docs/messages/blocking-prerender-metadata-runtime) and [Next.js encountered uncached data in `generateMetadata()`](/docs/messages/blocking-prerender-metadata-dynamic) for full fix options and trade-offs.
01335| 
01336| ### Ordering
01337| 
01338| Metadata is evaluated in order, starting from the root segment down to the segment closest to the final `page.js` segment. For example:
01339| 
01340| 1. `app/layout.tsx` (Root Layout)
01341| 2. `app/blog/layout.tsx` (Nested Blog Layout)
01342| 3. `app/blog/[slug]/page.tsx` (Blog Page)
01343| 
01344| ### Merging
01345| 
01346| Following the [evaluation order](#ordering), Metadata objects exported from multiple segments in the same route are **shallowly** merged together to form the final metadata output of a route. Duplicate keys are **replaced** based on their ordering.
01347| 
01348| This means metadata with nested fields such as [`openGraph`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/generate-metadata#opengraph) and [`robots`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/generate-metadata#robots) that are defined in an earlier segment are **overwritten** by the last segment to define them.
01349| 
01350| #### Overwriting fields
01351| 
01352| ```jsx filename="app/layout.js"
01353| export const metadata = {
01354|   title: 'Acme',
01355|   openGraph: {
01356|     title: 'Acme',
01357|     description: 'Acme is a...',
01358|   },
01359| }
01360| ```
01361| 
01362| ```jsx filename="app/blog/page.js"
01363| export const metadata = {
01364|   title: 'Blog',
01365|   openGraph: {
01366|     title: 'Blog',
01367|   },
01368| }
01369| 
01370| // Output:
01371| // <title>Blog</title>
01372| // <meta property="og:title" content="Blog" />
01373| ```
01374| 
01375| In the example above:
01376| 
01377| - `title` from `app/layout.js` is **replaced** by `title` in `app/blog/page.js`.
01378| - All `openGraph` fields from `app/layout.js` are **replaced** in `app/blog/page.js` because `app/blog/page.js` sets `openGraph` metadata. Note the absence of `openGraph.description`.
01379| 
01380| If you'd like to share some nested fields between segments while overwriting others, you can pull them out into a separate variable:
01381| 
01382| ```jsx filename="app/shared-metadata.js"
01383| export const openGraphImage = { images: ['http://...'] }
01384| ```
01385| 
01386| ```jsx filename="app/page.js"
01387| import { openGraphImage } from './shared-metadata'
01388| 
01389| export const metadata = {
01390|   openGraph: {
01391|     ...openGraphImage,
01392|     title: 'Home',
01393|   },
01394| }
01395| ```
01396| 
01397| ```jsx filename="app/about/page.js"
01398| import { openGraphImage } from '../shared-metadata'
01399| 
01400| export const metadata = {
01401|   openGraph: {
01402|     ...openGraphImage,
01403|     title: 'About',
01404|   },
01405| }
01406| ```
01407| 
01408| In the example above, the OG image is shared between `app/layout.js` and `app/about/page.js` while the titles are different.
01409| 
01410| #### Inheriting fields
01411| 
01412| ```jsx filename="app/layout.js"
01413| export const metadata = {
01414|   title: 'Acme',
01415|   openGraph: {
01416|     title: 'Acme',
01417|     description: 'Acme is a...',
01418|   },
01419| }
01420| ```
01421| 
01422| ```jsx filename="app/about/page.js"
01423| export const metadata = {
01424|   title: 'About',
01425| }
01426| 
01427| // Output:
01428| // <title>About</title>
01429| // <meta property="og:title" content="Acme" />
01430| // <meta property="og:description" content="Acme is a..." />
01431| ```
01432| 
01433| **Notes**
01434| 
01435| - `title` from `app/layout.js` is **replaced** by `title` in `app/about/page.js`.
01436| - All `openGraph` fields from `app/layout.js` are **inherited** in `app/about/page.js` because `app/about/page.js` doesn't set `openGraph` metadata.
01437|
